answer: Split the two things the case bundles together. A completed disposal-review decision -- a records officer on a given date deciding, for a stated reason, that a specific file is destroyed or kept permanently -- is a past act and could in principle be expressed with the CRM's generic assignment machinery: E13 Attribute Assignment carried out by the officer (P14), assigning the decision to the file (P140/P141), motivated by (P17 was motivated by) either an E30 Right (a statutory retention obligation) or a curator's judgement of significance. But the case is not really asking for that one historical fact -- it is asking to store the retention schedule itself and a standing 'next review date' alongside the file's description, i.e. a forward-looking scheduling/workflow field that drives a future administrative action. That is not something CIDOC CRM represents: the reference model states its own scope is 'curated, factual knowledge about the past', and explicitly puts 'information required solely for the administration and management of cultural institutions ... personnel, accounting, and visitor statistics' outside its Intended Scope -- a retention/disposal workflow is the same kind of institutional records-management housekeeping, not documentation of the past. The mailing list confirms the deeper reason: when the SIG considered adding a general 'plan for a future activity' construct (the 2009 Activity Plan proposal), Christian-Emil Ore's objection was that 'CRM is defined to be retrospective and not talk about the future', and the proposal did not become part of the model. So: describe the file itself, and (once it has happened) the disposal decision as a past event, in CRM terms if you need to cross-reference it into a documented history; but keep the retention schedule and the next-review-date trigger in the records-management/business system that actually runs the workflow -- do not try to make the CRM carry a future due-date.

rejected_alternatives.option: E29 Design or Procedure ("Activity Plan") as a home for the retention schedule/next review date
rejected_alternatives.why_not: The SIG discussed exactly this kind of future-oriented plan construct in the 2009 'Activity Plan' proposal (thread t0483) and Christian-Emil Ore rejected the future-tense framing on the grounds that 'CRM is defined to be retrospective and not talk about the future'; no such class exists in the current model, so there is no CRM home for a 'next review date' field.

rejected_alternatives.option: E87 Curation Activity for the disposal review
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E87 requires P147 curated -> E78 Curated Holding as its necessary property; it is scoped to the management of a collection as a whole, not a single file's retain/destroy decision, and still falls under 'management' of the holding rather than documentation about the past.

notes: The case conflates a one-off past decision (which the CRM's generic E13/P17 machinery could express) with a standing future-due-date schedule (which it explicitly cannot, per its own scope statement and the SIG's rejection of a general future-plan class). No search turned up an archives-specific or records-management extension of the CRM family that covers retention scheduling, so the 'different kind of system' side of the question is the honest answer for the scheduling half of the case.
